data.revised_prompt:
Edit the provided scientific figure into a clean, simplified publication-quality vector-style diagram for a paper titled “Differentiable active-depth model”. Preserve the left-to-right logical structure but greatly simplify the content and spacing. Use a white background, crisp black outlines, teal/gray section headers, and only minimal red gradient arrows for learning signals. Large readable labels only, no dense equations.

REQUIRED LAYOUT LEFT TO RIGHT:
1) Inputs / native geometry panel on the left:
- small active stereo sensing sketch (simple icon only)
- label: “Native renderer R → D_raw”
- label: “scene mask Ω”
- label: “speed ||v_t||”
- label: “camera registers c=[P,E,G]” with three visible chips: “P power”, “E exposure”, “G gain”

2) Central block:
- a large box labeled: “S_φ Differentiable active-depth sensor”
- inside or directly beneath it, show only five small factor chips:
  • “active return (P, range)”
  • “ambient washout (E, Ω)”
  • “motion blur (E, ||v_t||)”
  • “gain/noise (G)”
  • “edge difficulty (depth discontinuity)”
- these factor chips merge into a single output chip/label: “quality Q”

3) Validity and mask:
- show “soft validity M”
- show “straight-through mask: hard forward, soft backward”

4) Outputs on the right:
- “D_obs observed depth” with a simple grayscale thumbnail icon
- “Q_obs observed quality” with a simple heatmap thumbnail icon
- a small loss box: “L_sens / L_teach”

FORWARD FLOW:
- Use black arrows only.
- D_raw, Ω, speed, and c=[P,E,G] feed into S_φ / the factor chips.
- Q → M → D_obs and Q_obs.

BACKWARD FLOW:
- Use red arrows only.
- Draw a SHORT, clean red gradient path from “L_sens / L_teach” through Q/M/D_obs back to the camera registers c=[P,E,G].
- Add label on the red path: “gradient to P,E,G”.
- Absolutely do NOT draw red arrows to speed ||v_t||.
- Absolutely do NOT draw red arrows to Ω, D_raw, active stereo sketch, or renderer R.
- Include a gray note near the backprop path: “D_raw, Ω, speed, and R are fixed in sensor backward”.
- No long red bus along the bottom.

STYLE CONSTRAINTS:
- Less crowded than the original reference.
- Polished vector-like SCI journal style.
- No dense formulas or small unreadable panels.
- Keep the camera register chips P/E/G visible and distinct.
- Do not imply geometry-ray intersections are differentiable in this sensor branch.
- Ensure the gradient destination is only c=[P,E,G].

Make the diagram clean, balanced, and publication-ready.

Revise the scientific diagram to remove the long red bottom bus and make the backpropagation path short, local, and clean. Keep the same overall simplified layout and publication-quality vector style, but fix the learning signal flow as follows:

- The only red arrows should be a short path from the loss box “L_sens / L_teach” to the right-side outputs and then back to the camera register chips “c=[P,E,G]”.
- The red path should stay on the right half of the figure and connect only these nodes: L_sens / L_teach -> Q_obs / D_obs -> M -> Q -> camera registers c=[P,E,G].
- Add the red label “gradient to P,E,G” near this short path.
- Do NOT draw any red arrow across the bottom of the figure.
- Do NOT draw any red arrow under the speed box.
- Do NOT draw any red arrow to Ω, D_raw, the active stereo sketch, or renderer R.
- Keep the gray note: “D_raw, Ω, speed, and R are fixed in sensor backward”.

Keep all forward arrows black only.
Keep the title: “Differentiable active-depth model”.
Keep the left input panel, central S_φ sensor box with five factor chips, soft validity M, straight-through mask, observed depth and quality outputs, and visible P/E/G chips. Make the figure cleaner, with more whitespace and less clutter than before, and ensure the red gradient route is minimal and clearly constrained to P/E/G only.
